A retry with the same `idempotency_key` must use the same arguments, with `pgledger_create_transfers` requests in the same order (see Batch Ordering), or an error will be returned:

PostgreSQL has several transaction isolation levels. Under Read Committed (the default), concurrent calls with the same `idempotency_key` will wait for each other, and the later ones will return the transfers created from the first call if the requests match. Under Repeatable Read or Serializable, the later calls cannot see transfers created after the start of their own transaction snapshot. So instead of returning the existing transfers, the call will fail and should be re-tried in a new transaction.
For a more detailed example, see: examples/multi-currency.sql.out
IDs for all tables are represented as prefixed ULIDs, such as `pgla_01JTVST7XAES5BXHWZN4KR4VEZ` for a ledger account and `pglt_01JTVR1WKXEKCRG7N6YD7XCZA6` for a ledger transfer.
For more info about prefixed ULIDs as IDs, check out this blog post: ULID Identifiers and ULID Tools Website.

ULIDs are generated by first generating a UUIDv7>) (time-based, ordered UUID) and then converting that to a ULID via the SQL functions from https://github.com/scoville/pgsql-ulid (included in the vendor directory).
